title: Error Handling & Retry Strategies 🛡️
description: Catch HTTP errors gracefully and implement retry logic with RxJS operators.

slides.title: When Things Go Wrong 💥
slides.content:
# HTTP Errors Are Inevitable

Servers go down, networks fail, authentication expires. Angular’s `HttpClient` wraps errors in an `HttpErrorResponse` object.

You **must** handle errors – otherwise the Observable chain breaks and your component freezes.

RxJS provides `catchError` to gracefully handle errors and return a fallback Observable or throw a user‑friendly error.

slides.title: catchError Operator

quizData.question: Which RxJS operator is used to catch and handle errors in an Observable stream?
quizData.explanation: `catchError` intercepts errors and allows you to return a new Observable or rethrow.

slides.title: Retry Strategies ♻️
slides.content:
Transient network glitches can be solved by automatically retrying the request. RxJS provides:

* `retry(count)` – retry N times on error.
* `retryWhen(notifier)` – more sophisticated conditional retry.

```typescript
this.http.get('/api/data').pipe(
  retry(3)  // retry up to 3 times before failing
);
```
Be careful: retrying POST requests can cause duplicate writes unless the operation is idempotent.

slides.title: Retry with Delay ⚠️

quizData.question: It's safe to retry a POST request with `retry(2)` because POST is idempotent.
quizData.explanation: POST is not idempotent; retrying can create duplicate resources. Only retry safe methods like GET.
